subject: psychiatry
title: Persistent Delusional Disorder and Paranoid Syndromes

steps.tx: **Persistent delusional disorder** is characterized by the insidious development of a single well-systematized, non-bizarre delusion, or a group of related delusions, persisting for at least three months. Importantly, personality structure, intellect, and occupational functioning outside the direct sphere of the delusion remain remarkably preserved.
steps.say: Persistent delusional disorder involves stable, non-bizarre delusions lasting at least three months. General personality and functional capacity outside the delusion remain intact.

steps.tx: **Erotomania**, or de Clerambault syndrome, is a delusional subtype where the patient harbours an unshakeable conviction that another person, typically of higher socioeconomic standing or celebrity status, is secretly in love with them. The patient often interprets neutral media broadcasts, attire, or vehicle movements as covert romantic signals.
steps.say: Erotomania, or de Clerambault syndrome, is the conviction that an individual of higher social status is secretly in love with the patient, communicating through subtle signals.

left.title: de Clerambault Characteristics
points: Target of higher status or fame

steps.tx: **Othello syndrome**, also known as morbid jealousy or conjugal paranoia, involves an unfounded, fixed delusion that one's marital partner or romantic lover is unfaithful. Patients repeatedly interrogate spouses, search personal belongings, inspect bedsheets, and conduct intrusive surveillance, posing severe risks of domestic physical violence.
steps.say: Othello syndrome involves the unshakeable delusion that one's spouse is being unfaithful. Patients perform intrusive checks, which creates a substantial domestic violence hazard.

vis.title: Classic Delusional Subtypes
rows: Belief that high-status person loves patient; stalking
Unfounded spousal infidelity; severe violence risk
Belief that skin is infested by bugs; matchbox sign
Belief that organs or body are dead; severe depression

steps.tx: **Capgras syndrome** represents a delusional misidentification syndrome where the patient firmly believes that an emotionally significant person, such as a spouse or parent, has been replaced by an identical-looking imposter. It arises from neuroanatomical disconnection between intact facial recognition in the fusiform gyrus and emotional autonomic appraisal.
steps.say: In Capgras syndrome, the patient believes a close relative has been replaced by an identical double. It reflects disconnection between facial recognition and emotional familiarity.

left.title: Capgras Syndrome
points: Familiar person is deemed an imposter
More common in organic cerebral lesions

right.title: Fregoli Syndrome
points: Strangers identified as a familiar person

steps.tx: **Fregoli syndrome** is the converse delusional misidentification phenomenon, wherein the patient identifies completely unfamiliar strangers as a familiar persecutor disguised in different physical appearances. Patients believe this single antagonist systematically changes clothing, makeup, and bodily features to pursue and torment them in public environments.
steps.say: Fregoli syndrome causes patients to believe strangers are actually a single familiar persecutor disguised in different bodies to surveil and torment them.

nodes.label: Visual face recognition via fusiform gyrus
Capgras: Loss of limbic autonomic emotional signal produces double delusion
Fregoli: Limbic hyper-reactivity falsely attaches familiarity to strangers

steps.tx: **Cotard syndrome** involves profound nihilistic delusions wherein patients assert that they have lost their internal organs, have no blood, have died, or that the entire world has ceased to exist. Classically encountered in severe psychotic depression, it carries extreme suicide risk and severe self-neglect.
steps.say: Cotard syndrome features nihilistic delusions of being dead or lacking internal organs. It occurs in severe melancholic psychotic depression and requires urgent electroconvulsive therapy.

left.title: Nihilistic Symptomatology
points: Belief of having no blood, heart, or brain
Delusion that the patient is already dead
Belief that the external world is destroyed

right.title: Clinical Setting & Treatment
points: High risk of lethal starvation and suicide
Treatment of choice is bilateral ECT

steps.tx: **Schizoaffective disorder** requires the simultaneous presence of full psychotic symptoms meeting schizophrenia criteria alongside a prominent major depressive or manic episode. Critically, definitive diagnosis demands delusions or hallucinations persisting for at least two consecutive weeks in the complete absence of prominent affective symptoms.
steps.say: Schizoaffective disorder requires concurrent schizophrenia and mood episodes, with hallucinations or delusions persisting for at least two weeks without prominent mood symptoms.

steps.tx: **Shared psychotic disorder**, historically designated folie a deux, occurs when a secondary impressionable individual develops delusional beliefs transmitted directly from a dominant primary partner suffering from established psychotic illness. Management requires immediate physical separation of the pair, which frequently dissolves the delusional convictions of the secondary partner.
steps.say: Folie a deux describes delusion transmission from a dominant psychotic patient to an isolated partner. Physical separation often rapidly resolves delusions in the secondary individual.

nodes.label: Dominant inducer transmits delusion to submissive dependent
Shared social isolation reinforces mutual belief system
Physical separation of the pair in different environments
Secondary partner delusions resolve without major antipsychotic dosing
